claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys relative to a disordered solid solution.
The conductivity suppression caused by SRO exceeds the effect of atomic mass variance alone.
SRO introduces resonant phonon-scattering centers that broaden the phonon spectrum.
The baseline lattice thermal conductivity of the disordered alloy is dominated by point-defect scattering arising from atomic mass and size differences.
A homogenized CrCoNi sample can lack detectable chemical short-range order.
Thermal aging at approximately 1200 K can induce nanometer-scale local chemical order without causing precipitation or long-range phase separation.
Ni-Cr pairing is a possible local chemical-order motif in CrCoNi.
Aging can develop SRO while retaining a single-phase FCC or BCC crystal structure.
Between 300 K and 800 K, phonon-phonon scattering is significant but not dominant in the proposed refractory alloys.
SRO produces nanometer-scale ordered domains with specific pair correlations and associated local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions around ordered domains act as resonant scattering centers for mid-to-high-frequency phonons.
Ordered clusters possess vibrational modes different from those of the random matrix and therefore cause resonant phonon scattering.
Strain fields surrounding ordered domains broaden the phonon spectrum and reduce phonon group velocity and mean free path.
The reduction in lattice thermal conductivity scales with the degree of SRO.
Electron diffuse streaks along {111} have been reported in CrCoNi.
The intensity of diffuse diffraction streaks provides a quantitative measure of SRO degree.
Long-range ordering or phase separation would introduce grain boundaries or secondary phases as the dominant phonon-scattering mechanism.
SRO or local chemical order affects mechanical properties, dislocation behavior, and stacking-fault energy in CrCoNi or related concentrated solid solutions.
General HEA literature establishes phonon-spectrum broadening relevant to the proposed SRO transport mechanism.

contradictions.description: The study is framed as concerning refractory HEAs, but CoCrFeMnNi is offered as an example refractory test alloy even though the conventional CoCrFeMnNi alloy is not a refractory HEA.
